## The Olympic Games

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- The first recorded {{< vocab "Olympic Games" >}} were in **776 BC**, at Olympia.
- They were held every **four years**, to honor Zeus.
- Athletes came from many {{< vocab "city-state" text="city-states" >}}.
- The oldest event was a running race, about 190 meters.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{python}
#| output: asis
print(card_grid(pick(terms, "Olympic Games"), zh=True, notes=True))
```
:::
::::

::: notes
The modern Olympics started in 1896 in Athens, copying the ancient idea.
:::

## Gods and myths

- The Greeks believed the most important gods lived on **Mount Olympus**.
- A {{< vocab "myth" >}} is a story about gods and heroes. Myths explained thunder, the seasons and the sea.

| God | In charge of | 中文 |
|---|---|---|
| Zeus | the sky and thunder; king of the gods | 宙斯 |
| Athena | wisdom; protector of Athens | 雅典娜 |
| Poseidon | the sea and earthquakes | 波塞冬 |

::: notes
The Greek Gods fact cards (reference) have three more gods, and a blank card to design your own.
:::

## Thinkers who asked big questions

::: {.timeline}
- **Socrates** · Taught by asking questions: *What is fair? What is a good life?*
- **Plato** · Socrates' student. Wrote down his teacher's ideas and started a school.
- **Aristotle** · Plato's student. Studied everything from animals to government.
:::

A {{< vocab "philosopher" >}} is a thinker who asks big questions about life and truth.

## Temples and columns

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
- The Parthenon is a {{< vocab "temple" >}} to Athena, on the Acropolis hill in Athens.
- Its roof rested on rows of a {{< vocab "column" >}} style called Doric.
- Greek {{< vocab "column" text="columns" >}} came in three styles.
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{python}
#| output: asis
print(card_grid(pick(terms, "temple", "column"), zh=True))
```
:::
::::

::: notes
Ask: where in our city have you seen columns like these? (Banks, museums, government buildings.)
:::

## Theater

- Greek plays were tragedies (sad endings) or comedies (funny).
- Actors wore masks, so one actor could play many characters.
- The {{< vocab "theater" >}} was built into a hillside: everyone could see and hear.

::: {.small-note}
English words from Greek theater: *drama*, *scene*, *chorus*, *comedy*, *tragedy*.
:::
